summary: [FAIL] One Blocking issue found: FfmpegProvisioningOptions.Manifest property is typed as Dictionary<string, ToolManifestEntry> but the plan spec explicitly defines it as IReadOnlyDictionary<string, ToolManifestEntry>. This exposes a mutable collection type for configuration data that should be read-only after initialization. All other new types are architecturally sound — 5 interfaces, 2 enums, 3 models, 2 options records, and 1 event args class are all clean. Code style, XML docs, and project conventions are consistently followed. One Documentation-Forward item tagged for the Documentation agent.

comments.note: BLOCKING — FfmpegProvisioningOptions.Manifest typed as mutable Dictionary. The plan spec (plan.md line ~203) explicitly defines this property as IReadOnlyDictionary<string, ToolManifestEntry>. The implementation uses Dictionary<string, ToolManifestEntry>, which allows callers to mutate the manifest dictionary after initialization (e.g., adding or removing RID entries). This violates the intended immutability of configuration data: the `init`-only accessor prevents reassigning the property reference, but does not prevent dict.Add()/dict.Remove() on the existing instance. Fix: change the property declaration to `public IReadOnlyDictionary<string, ToolManifestEntry> Manifest { get; init; } = new Dictionary<string, ToolManifestEntry>();` The collection expression `= []` must also change to `= new Dictionary<string, ToolManifestEntry>()` since `[]` is not supported for interface types.

ProvisioningOutcome (public enum, Core) is not wired into any interface contract. The plan architecture section specifies `EnsureAsync → ToolPaths` (which the implementation correctly follows), but the provisioner algorithm description informally says 'return AlreadyPresent/Downloaded' — an internal contradiction in the plan. The Developer made a defensible choice (Task<ToolPaths>). However, ProvisioningOutcome is currently a public Core type with no consumers. The next WP (Infrastructure implementation) should clarify: if ProvisioningOutcome is used only inside FfmpegProvisioner for internal logging/branching, change its accessibility to `internal`. If it is intended to surface to callers, update IExternalToolProvisioner to return a result wrapper. Not blocking this WP, but must be decided before the Infrastructure WP starts.

[documentation-forward] ExternalToolsOptions.cs is missing a class-level <summary> XML doc comment. The three pre-existing properties (VlcExecutablePath, MySqlBinaryFolder, ExternalXmlEditorPath) and the new Ffmpeg property all have individual docs, but the sealed record itself has no type-level description explaining its role as the options section for all external tool binary locations.

IArchiveExtractor.ExtractAsync has no ArchiveType parameter — confirmed as intentional by plan design (CompositeArchiveExtractor dispatches by file extension/archive type internally). Correct pattern.

Minor naming asymmetry: ToolPaths.Version vs FfmpegToolOptions.ResolvedVersion. The two types serve distinct purposes (runtime provisioning result vs persisted config cache), so different naming is acceptable and arguably clearer. No action required.
